Question: Lines \(AB\) and \(CD\) intersect at point \(O\). Given \(\angle AOC=4x-15^\circ\) and \(\angle BOD=2x+35^\circ\), find the measure of \(\angle AOC\) in degrees.
Solution:
The statement places \(A,B,O\) on one line and \(C,D,O\) on another, but does not specify the point order. Thus \(OA,OB\) can be the same ray or opposite rays, and likewise for \(OC,OD\).

If both pairs are opposite rays, the named angles are vertical and equal. If both pairs are the same ray, the named angles coincide and are again equal. In either case,
\[
4x-15=2x+35,
\]
so \(x=25\) and \(\angle AOC=4\times25-15=85^\circ\).

If exactly one pair is opposite, the named angles are supplementary. Therefore
\[
(4x-15)+(2x+35)=180,
\]
which gives \(6x=160\), \(x=80/3\), and
\[
\angle AOC=\left(\frac{275}{3}\right)^\circ.
\]
This case is possible with \(A,B\) on opposite sides of \(O\) and \(C,D\) on the same ray; the other angle is \((265/3)^\circ\), so both angles are valid.

These cases exhaust the same-ray and opposite-ray possibilities. Hence the displayed question has no unique answer: \(85^\circ\) follows under the intended opposite-ray arrangement, while another permitted arrangement gives \((275/3)^\circ\).
